ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating a block
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ian, First, you say you are "going to the Admin section". However for blocks to update, you need to go to the Notifications link (in Moodle 1.9+ anyway). I know, that is not an obvious place to go, but that is what triggers the check for updates. If you have done that, then read on. What is the reason for updating? Are you trying to update the database table your block uses (e.g. you changed the schema)? The reason I ask is because in my block development, I have only been concerned about Moodle recognizing a version change if I have changed my database tables. I only started working on blocks a couple of months ago, so my experience is still limited. Perhaps these sites will help, if you haven't seen them yet: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Installing_and_upgrading_plugin_database_tables One thing to note about the above site is with blocks, I have not required the version.php file for the upgrade to occur. Also, note that in the reference to the upgrade function, the $oldversion parameter gets a default value of 0. The second reference here below does not say that, so don't be confused. There is also a bit of information here: http://docs.moodle.org/en/index.php?title=XMLDB_editor The part that was not obvious to me until I worked through these references was the link between PHP code generated by XMLDB, where that should go, and block version numbers. Now, if your issue has nothing to do with a database table , then really your code should be updated to the new behaviour as soon as you change it. So if you are having an issue with that, perhaps you need to provide a few more details. I will ask the first obvious questions that we all often miss: Are the files you think you are changing in the correct file structure location for Moodle to run them? Are you saving the files before testing behaviour? Are you refreshing the browser? I know, sorry to have to ask, but anyone can miss those sometimes! Carvell

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating a block
ResponsesInList.Text: Ian, One other thought: I jumped to the conclusion that you were doing block development because you mentioned changing the version number. If you are just trying to install and update other people's blocks, then the code to handle the version update should be included in the files with the block. If it is not, then this would be a good question for the block developer. Also, I don't know if you could have issues with permissions on the block folders. I am running on Windows and am an admin on my test and deployment PCs, so that has not been an issue for me. However there may be required permission changes if you're running Moodle on a Linux server . Carvell

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blocks disappear when moving from left to right.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I've found a silly bug that was resulting in same effect : The fix is : in lib/blockslib.php function blocks_get_by_page($page) { $blocks = get_records_select('block_instance', "pageid = '". $page->get_id() . "' AND pagetype = '". $page->get_type() ."'", 'position, weight'); $positions = $page->blocks_get_positions(); $arr = array(); foreach($positions as $key => $position) { $arr[$position] = array(); } if(empty($blocks)) { return $arr; } foreach($blocks as $block) { // very important fix. Fixes lost blocks in flexipage and front page format // renumbers the duplicate weights in order... while (array_key_exists($block->weight, $arr[$block->position])){ $block->weight++; update_record('block_instance', $block); } $arr[$block->position][$block->weight] = $block; } return $arr; } Maybe it has something to do with the error you're experimenting. It fixed all weird behaviour definitively in our instances. I'll seek for a tracker entry... may help. Problem is that some block moves do not calculate correctly the weight of the landing block, and weight duplicates appear in database. This fix recalculates dynamically the weights of the blocks in the page so they are in correct order, and no one is forgotten. Beware : you may have some ghosts reviving !! Cheers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What all does the Elgg integration do?
ResponsesInList.Text: Mark, the main point of the integration between moodle and elgg is for authentication. Depending on your actual usage scenarios, moodle and elgg are quite orthogonal. I know moodle is moving more into the social sphere with blogs, but currently elgg is meant to be a student centered space, while moodle fulfils the actual elearning component. Also, don't forget that you can have elgg as an overarching social system that more than one moodle can plug into. This means you could have an elgg that gets users fed to it from all moodles within a school district. In keeping moodle and elgg as separate spaces, this also means that accounts, once created in elgg, can be kept across any number of moodles, and for a longer period than just attendance at once school, they can span a student's whole academic life. On to the actual integration. Yes, the file sharing is quite basic at the moment. However, it was written in such a way that it's just a matter of adding a couple of module functions to whatever activity module you want, to allow it to expose files to export. If you have good ideas about how you'd like it extended, feel free to write a patch Also it's worth mentioning that there's a whole raft of issues here around plagiarism. Currently with the assignment module integration, you can only export files once the assignment is closed, and the submission has been graded. Even so, many institutions will choose not to use it because they reuse assessment structure across semesters/years/class intakes. The integration may not fit your usage scenario. That's ok, part of the whole thing with using open source is that you have the choice. You can use parts of it you find useful, or not if you want. It certainly fits our scenario in NZ for the NZVLE project, where we have a number of tertiaries (so far I think there's just tertiaries, but potentially highschools too) who have their distinct moodles plugging into it for authentication and user accounts. As users go through their school/university life (and transfer between different institutions), they can use the same account at the same external portfolio system that isn't aligned with their institution. Maybe that clears up some of the expectations. At any rate, in the spirit of open source and collaboration, if you have programmer resource available to add functionality to the moodle/elgg integration, the code is there in contrib as a starting point

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What all does the Elgg integration do?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, I have to confess... it's a bit hard to put all our work up for people to use for free, and then be asked "is that all?". So I don't know really what the answer to your question is. However, I've worked with Penny in the design and implementation of Elgg/Moodle integration. We did quite a bit of work in the plan and design, and we had goals... and constraints. Here's a bit of a list: Single Sign On. It works. (Niiiiice, I say). Signup to Elgg can be restricted to come from Moodle. This is really important for institutions that want to run Elgg as a portfolio or a social environment. Elgg is under their control in terms of access and account creation can be tied to existing and valid Moodle accounts. Assumes valid students have Moodle accounts somehow (via a suitable auth plugin, for instance). A powerful non-course-centric blog that is more Blog-like. In general, an environment that is themed separately from Moodle to show it is a clearly different "social space". One Elgg can be used as a service for many different Moodle installs. This is what runs behind http://myportfolio.ac.nz/ . In this context , Elgg is on one hand portfolio, and on the other social space. Arguably the portfolio is nascent, but the social space is very developed (that's what Elgg is). Some limited integration to transfer your content around. A bit more about why it is limited... It raises concerns: as Penny mentions above, teachers will want to control publishing of stuff submitted to courses. It is hard to transfer content "transparently" across servers. And we need it to run across servers. We got this sorted out well (sftp, keys, the whole thing), but it took quite a bit of work. It is hard to transfer module-specific content. A lot of stuff in Moodle is "content" that only the moodle module knows how to lay out. How do you export your quiz answers without the quiz engine? Wiki pages without the Wiki engine? All of this needs quite a bit of coding per module. As you can see, resources are scarce -- we are under pressure to achieve a lot with very little time. So we are forced to be ruthless in our decisionmaking here. Our Elgg-Moodle work hasn't finished, not has our interest and involvement in portfolios and social spaces. We keep working on it, but bear in mind it is not a mature space like LMSs (not everyone agrees what a portfolio is) and Elgg is not as mature as Moodle is. It's all evolving, and we keep working. And we want feedback -- so thanks for your comments. However... there is a lot of noise and we have to focus on the useful feedback. Armchair criticism scores much, much lower than practical usage stuff we can fix in small steps. Come tell us something like "I am using it with a bunch of (teachers/students/researchers/hamsters) and we found feature X useful and feature Y not so practical". Or stuff like "specific bug Z gets really in the way". Helping is not just for programmers -- it is for people ready to get involved and spend quality time working things out. It not trivial to provide constructive criticism that is practical and useful to us. We work in short, simple steps, aiming for concrete goals; we release early and often. This is the first of what I hope will be a long series of "release early and often" Moodle/Elgg combos. It works and achieves all the (humble) goals we set out to meet. Colour me satisfied with that at least But I agree with you, there's a lot more to be done, and there's room for people to help shape where this goes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What all does the Elgg integration do?
ResponsesInList.Text: Martin and Penny, I apologize for coming across as a critic. You and the other developers have done a lot of hard work for nothing but the love of it and the desire to give--and I appreciate both the intent and the results. I like to say that I don't give excuses, just explanations. So let me explain. My attitude, which I admit was inconsiderate and undeserved, arose from the fact that I got involved in Elgg before I got involved in Moodle. I came from the perspective of enhancing Elgg rather than complementing Moodle. The integration was much touted over on elgg.net and, in my admitted ignorance of eportfolios and lmss, I developed a picture of what to expect that overreached the current state of development. As I mentioned to Penny, I know just a dabbling little bit about what goes on behind the interface, so I am apt to expect more than I might if I knew how things worked. I have found a few php reference resources on the Internet and have begun studying them. I want to be a developer, too. Penny's challenge in that regard was more than fair. I have big plans, as you might imagine, but I'll start small and, if you guys don't leave me too far behind, cut some of my later teeth on your project. I'm particularly interested in having in-course blog posts export to Elgg. I'd like to learn more about the restricted signup. How does that work? And how do you link more than one moodle with a single elgg? Again, my apologies to both you and Penny (and any other developers I've offended). I really do appreciate the work and the results. I just have to get a clearer picture of the work involved and the kinds of results that are reasonable to expect. This discussion has helped a lot in that vein.

By completing this basic implementation I have identified some future implementations or extensions to this block to get the maximum use of it, such as Improve the ranking algorithms, so that each activity can have a different weights attached to them. Cheers, Chad

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Clickatell SMS Block
ResponsesInList.Text: I had problems with the HTML Editor not appearing, caused by the mod_security module of Apache being over-zealous. When I fixed that, the SMS block started working for me .  The following page explains some of the background: http://www.urbangiraffe.com/2005/08/20/mysterious-406-error/ So, try the following... if there is not one already, create a file called ".htaccess" file add the following lines to disable mod_security: <IfModule mod_security.c> /mod_security.c> SecFilterEngine Off SecFilterScanPOST Off </IfModule> If that solves the problem, then I would stringly advise you to contact your web host and get them to tweak and tone down the security, rather than leaving the mod_security module disabled. There's more information about the mod_security module at http://www.modsecurity.org/

ResponsesInList.Title: Does it have to be so bloody complicated? (preferred_width)
ResponsesInList.Text: I am working on Development:Very flexible block system proposal , part of the Moodle 2.0 navigation/themes/etc. changes; and I am looking at the bit where it computes the width of each column of blocks, and thinking "does it really have to be this complicated". Here is how it currently works: Moodle works out which blocks will be visible in, say, the left column. It then asks each of those blocks what it's 'preferred_width' is. ( At this point, almost every block answers 180(px), looking through core code and contrib, other responses (with number of blocks that give that response) are 210 (8), 250 (2), 210 (2), 170 (1), 140 (1) ) Then it asks the theme if it wants to put any limit of the size of the blocks columns. Most themes use the default min = 100, max = 210. The two exceptions in core+contrib are anomaly: min = max = 200, and customcorners: min = max = 180. - Oh, except for the places where it does not bother the consult the theme, and instead hard-codes min = 180, max = 210. Then Moodle computes the actual width of the column as max(preferred widths from 2), but limited to be within the min and max given by the theme. What does Moodel actually do with this number? Well, if this is a page that is still using horrible old-style tables for layout, then that width in pixels goes on the td for that blocks column as a style="width: NNNpx;" attribute. However, on pages that have been converted to divs, like course/format/weeks/format.php, then that number is ignored, and instead in the theme we have .weeks-format #left-column { width: 11.5em; } in the theme CSS .

ResponsesInList.Text: I'm happy with any effort to simplify something that should be as simple as block widths. If this could help the admin pages, all the better

ResponsesInList.Text: The less the better! Layout is the responsibility of the theme.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does it have to be so bloody complicated? (preferred_width)
ResponsesInList.Text: I think blocks should be still be allowed to specify a preferred width in pixels if they want to. Moodle should take all those and boil it down to one number which it makes available to the theme. The theme can then do what it wants with that info (including ignoring it). IMO the existing div-based course formats should use that number - it's a bug that they don't.

ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with the idea that ems rather than px width sounds like a good goal. In the Docs: "That means that the width setting is a best-effort settlement; your block can request a certain width and Moodle will try to provide it, but there's no guarantee whatsoever about the end result. As a concrete example, all standard Moodle course formats will deliver any requested width between 180 and 210 pixels, inclusive. " http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Blocks How should that be "ems" rephrased? It would seem good to have all blocks, and themes, descriptions include what width they need, respectively which block widths they will support.

I don't think background images resize (except browsers that use a "zoom" technique for resizing like Firefox ). --- More to the point of your question, I think it's important to have predictable results. I have a course where the instructor has a randomly generated post from a wiki appearing on the course page in a column. It drives me nuts that the column keeps resizing depending on the content that gets ported into it (long urls that don't break and other things). Sometimes the page displays beautifully and other times it expands squishes the center column which has the main content, reads very poorly, and looks like a mistake. regards, Ian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does it have to be so bloody complicated? (preferred_width)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, I do not have a solution but I remember that one of the problems with CSS only course formats was that you need to specify widths for the side columns, and the layout would get mucked up completely if one of the blocks was larger than this width. Ideally a fixed width maximum for all blocks would solve this,sort of, but then you will get problems such as when a teacher places a wide image in a HTML block. Unless there is a mechanism for preventing this you will always end up with a potential problem. On my site I use max-width CSS rules for images in blocks that sort of prevent this but it does not prevent images having wrong aspect ratios and only catches this one circumstance. After typing the above I do think that the best solution may be that the block width needs to be a value specified by the theme that all blocks must adhere to, especially with the planned changes to themes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where are HTML blocks stored?
ResponsesInList.Text: The data for each block (including the HTML block) is serialized, then base64encoded and stored inside the configdata field of the mdl_block_instance table. That's why it will be hard to write a mysql query to backup/restore a lot of HTML blocks at once. If you know PHP you can use unserialize(base64_decode($instance->configdata))

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Administration block for studetns
ResponsesInList.Text: I have implemented something like what Ingo is trying to do, but I am not sure it would work for Joe. I wanted to make users with a very restricted set of permissions, so I duplicated the roles that I thought were closest to what I wanted, and then modified the duplicate permissions and took away all the things I didn't want that role to be able to do. Then, when assigning roles within a context , I assigned my new role to the user rather than the Moodle default (e.g. rather than assign a student the Moodle Student role in a course, I assigned my new Student role). I would not recommend modifying the Moodle default roles. According to what I have read in the Moodle docs and various tutorials, it is generally a bad idea to mess with the defaults. Always good to keep them just in case. Of course it is open source, so feel free to do what you want! I did this all though the Users -> Permissions -> Define roles page in Moodle. If you go to that page, then click on the Role that you want to duplicate (click on its hyperlinked name), you will get a page that has a "Duplicate role" button. Duplicate the role, then edit the new role's permissions. I have been able to tailor pretty much exactly what I want each user to have access to in each context. Be warned: there are a lot of permissions, and it may take some trial and error to get the combination that you want, but it has worked for me. Perhaps that would be a way to do it for you rather than overriding permissions. I did all this in version 1.9.4, and that's the only version I have used so far. Carvell

ResponsesInList.Title: Help for others: Confusion with Blocks and applicable_formats function
ResponsesInList.Text: Just thought I would pass this along in case anyone else working on blocks gets confused. When you are working with the applicable_formats function, what you are actually setting, based on my observations, is whether or not your block will be available in the Blocks dropdown list in a given page context when editing is turned on. Why does that matter? If you have already added your block to a page, setting the value for that page to false in applicable_formats does not remove the existing instance from the page. For example, if you have added the simpleHTML block to a course page while completing the blocks tutorial, and then try modifying the applicable_formats function to set that your block should not be visibile on course pages, the change will not remove the one(s) you added previously in the tutorial. It will only prevent you from adding another from the Blocks dropdown. If you remove all the instances of your block, and then turn editing on, you will see that setting the applicable_formats array controls whether or not your block appears in the Blocks dropdown for the pages you have specified, and therefore whether or not you can add it to those pages going forward. Maybe that was not confusing for anyone else, but I thought I would share. I was thinking that if I set false for a page in applicable_formats, all the instances of that block would be removed, but that is not the case. Carvell

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Global Search - xPDF!
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the help - I was able to figure this one out. It was a permission/IIS setup issue, here's the fix I found: Under the IIS MMC, I went to "Information and Internet Services"-->"Web Sites" and right clicked on the moodle site, and then chose "Properties". ResponsesInList.Text: Ok - doing a Lewis Carroll White Queen and screaming before my finger was pricked - working on it a bit more, I found I can just call the global $USER and then access $USER->custom_field_name sorry to bother you all cheers -- Tony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Displaying custom profile fields in a block
ResponsesInList.Text: I had a message asking how I did this, so I thought it would be better to put it here so that anyone can see (and correct, if what I've said is either inaccurate or bad practice!) I'm assuming anyone reading this is ok with the basics of building a block (as shown at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Blocks ) So... in the block content section of your block's php file, you need some code along the lines of the following: function get_content() { global $USER; // you need this line to be able to use the global array "$USER" within this function if ($this->content !== NULL) { return $this->content; } $this->content = new stdClass; $this->content->text = 'Favourite colour: '.$USER->favcolour; // I haven't worked out how to get the field description dynamically displayed, so I've just hard coded the text to explain the field (i.e. "Favourite colour: "). The "favcolour" bit of "$USER->favcolour" is the unique name you gave your custom profile field when you set it up in the Users > Profile fields section of the site administration. This bit of code simply asks for the "favcolour" entry in the global $USER array. As it stand here, this block only displays a single line of text, so in practice I'm sure you would want to combine it with other stuff. $this->content->footer = ''; return $this->content; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Custom Blocks on all courses by default
ResponsesInList.Text: I have just created a couple of blocks, i would like these to run through the whole site, not just the front page , and be placed in the same order on each course. We have already got alot of courses on our site, so manually adding these to each course is only a last option. Can this be done? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom Blocks on all courses by default
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ed, First of all, what you need to do depends on what version of Moodle you use. I assume 1.4.x. Second, you will need to do a little customized programming to achieve the desired effect. Every course in Moodle corresponds to one record in table mdl_course in the database . This table contains a "blockinfo" field which holds the information about the blocks in each course. The blockinfo field in general has the format A,B,...,C:X,Y,...,Z where A, B, C, X, Y, Z etc are numbers which correspond to block ids from the mdl_block table (you can see in that table which number corresponds to which block). The double colon separates left:right blocks. If a number is negative, e.g. -3, this means that in that position we have the block with id = 3 but it is hidden. Now what you need to do is write a small script that loops over all the records in mdl_course, takes the blockinfo field, does a little string manipulation in order to insert your new block ids in the required place, and then calls update_record or something equivalent to write the data back to the db. I hope this helps to get you started!

Okay then, let's add invisibility but also make the fix a little bit more flexible. Create a text file and add to it the following lines: // detect edit mode var arTmp=document.getElementsByTagName("body"); var theBody=arTmp[0]; var editMode=theBody.className.search(/editing/gi); // Hide blocks when not in editing if (editMode==-1) { // style definitions block document.getElementById("inst------").style.display="none"; } Again, substitute ------ for the instance id number of your definitions block. The block will be visible only when the page is in editing mode. Add to the file those style definitions you currently have in the block: var styleHtml; styleHtml+=''; if(document.getElementById("myStyles")){ document.getElementById("myStyles").innerHTML=styleHtml; } And as you can see you can add as many styles as you want. Save the file with suffix js (e.g. myStyles.js) and upload it to the course/site Files. Now you go back to the html block and in text mode clear its content and add the following lines:
Substitute ------------------- for your js file path. Save and close. For modifying the styles you don't have to open the block. You simply go to the file, edit it, make the desired changes and save. ResponsesInList.Title: New html role specific block
ResponsesInList.Text: I have re-written the html role specific block. The block was in a pretty poor state previously and had tons of inconsistent behaviour. I have correct all the inconsistencies but ran into as issue when working with the My Moodle page. My Moodle does not currently have any roles/contexts associated with it. This made it difficult to handle a role specific block placed on the My Moodle page (sticky or not) since there was nothing to check against! I came up with two options as solutions: 1. Have the block check against the Front Page roles as if they were assigned to the My Moodle page for blocks that are on that page. This is almost a logical solution since My Moodle usually takes the place of the Front Page (at least for logged in users) when enabled. This option is very simple and requires no extra modifications other than installing the third party block itself. This version of the block is just like any other block and can be found here: HTML Role specific block 2. Implement the roles system on the My Moodle page. This seems like a pretty big change to implement for a simple functionality only used by one type of block. The modifications required for this option were much more extensive and included changes to about 5 files. I went ahead and developed this solution anyway since I plan on eventually extending the role-specific functionality to all blocks. I've also written a script to apply the changes to make it easier for those less technically inclined. I would love some feedback on what people think about My Moodle roles and whether they feel it is necessary or not. This version requires a patch to be applied (run script) and can be found here: My Moodle patch & HTML role specific block

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Creation block
ResponsesInList.Text: The way this block displays information depends on who is viewing it. A student will not see the block. Anyone who has a teacher role in any course will see a link to request a course. An administrator will see a link to approve any existing course requests - but if there aren't any, they will see a message telling them that there aren't any requests to approve. You can test this with the Login As function - browse to different users and login as that user, and you will see what they see. Thanks, Matt

http://www.baker-evans.com/community

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Show Block on Frontpage based on login
ResponsesInList.Text: Sure. Assuming your default role is 'Authenticated user', turn editing on and click the roles icon on the block that you want shown only to logged in users. Select the Override roles tab and choose the Guest role. Set the View block capability to Prevent. Now only logged in users will see that block. If you want a block to show only to non-logged in users, override the Authenticated user role on that block and set View block to prevent.

These are; $string['questionbank'] = 'Question bank'; $string['questiondesc'] = 'Clicking this link will allow you access the question bank from where you can edit all quiz questions. Note that you cannot change anything about the actual quizzes here - for that go into the actual quiz'; Hope someone finds this as useful as I have found other hacks/solutions to problems. Also, I am not a programmer so cannot support what I have done - sorry. It works for me, that's all I can say - the best I can do is to pass it into the community for someone clever to run with. Thanks again to the original developers - great work!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: block n00b question
ResponsesInList.Text: Alastair - My apologies for not responding sooner. I am playing catch up this week and I had filed your question in my folder of things to follow up on. Your question is actually not a trivial one but does demonstrate that we need to update the documentation and the NEWBLOCK code so that it gives a good example. In Moodle 1.8 you would use $this->content->text to print the text; however, it looks like that was deprecated in Moodle 1.9 so that now you use the $this->content->items[] array instead. The function will still accept the $this->content->text string; however, it is ignored when actually generating the block. So here is what I would suggest for an ultra simple block as of Moodle 1.9: class block_hellouser extends block_list { function init() { $this->title = get_string('blockname','block_hellouser'); $this->version = 20080709; } function get_content() { if($this->content !== NULL) { return $this->content; } $this->content = new stdClass; $this->content->items = array(); $this->content->items[] = 'Item 1'; $this->content->items[] = 'Item 2'; // you can continue to add items to the block $this->content->icons = array(); $this->content->footer = 'Footer here...'; return $this->content; } } Let me know if you have questions about trying to use other information for $COURSE, $CFG, or other global variables. Peace - Anthony p.s. - I'm attaching a screen shot of how this looks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: block n00b question

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: block n00b question
ResponsesInList.Text: Dave - You have to keep in mind which class you are extending. In the code you sent, you were extending the class block_base and then creating a list. There is a separate class which has a separate _print_block function defined in /blocks/moodleblock.class.php. The block_base class requires that the text be defined as: $this->content->text = 'Hello world'; For a list, you change the line at the top to: class block_helloworld extends block_list { and then use: $this->content->items = 'Hello'; $this->content->items = 'world'; I found this by turning debugging on and it showed me that your original function was trying to call the block_class _print_block function and errored because the variable $this->content->text had not been defined. In your file, simply changing the class from block_base to block_list resolves the problem. Let me know if you have any other questions. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding homemade blocks in 1.9.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunate PHP mistakes can be a major hassle to root out sometimes. However, if you (temporarily) activate debug messages, then the system should help you find them. From the Admin menu, click " Server -> Debugging". In the "Debug Message" drop-down box, select, "ALL", and tick the checkbox below which says "Display debug messages". Save changes, and then try your block again. Hopefully, any major issues should show up, such as syntax errors of unrecognised functions and so on. After you have solved the problems though, it is quite important to turn the debug messages off again. If no error messages show up, but your block is still not noticed by Moodle, then you need to check your code and naming conventions. Look at existing blocks, such as the "admin" block (you'll find it in the "blocks/admin" folder). The PHP script is called "block_admin.php", and the class inside it is called "block_admin". Also note that it inherits from the "block_list" class (although you can use "block_base" instead). Make sure you block follows the same naming conventions. For example, if your block is called "foo", then the names would be as follows: Folder: "blocks/foo" PHP file: "block_foo.php" PHP class: "block_foo"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Connecting to a database within a block
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume you are just wanting to connect to the same database that all the Moodle data is already stored in? In that case, there is no need to do anything to make the connection, as Moodle is already connected to it. You just need to use Moodle's database-independent functions, such as "get_records" (or "get_records_sql" if you absolutely have to use your own SQL) and so on. They will usually return a database record as an object, or a numeric array of such objects. (Or false if the query fails). You can see the documentation for the functions at: http://phpdocs.moodle.org/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AJAX/HIJAX Calendar Block
ResponsesInList.Text:
There's a file called `lib/javascript.php` which controls the javascript includes in the head section of your Moodle pages. You'll find lines like: 
```text
<script language="JavaScript" type="text/javascript" src="<?php echo $CFG->httpswwwroot ?>/lib/overlib.js"></script>
```
 which you can copy and change to include the required files (listed in a post above) e.g. 
```text
<script language="JavaScript" type="text/javascript" src="<?php echo $CFG->httpswwwroot ?>/lib/yui/yahoo/yahoo.js"></script>
```
 (ignore the extra X added by Moodle for security reasons) As Jan mentions there are 'compressed' or 'minified' versions of each file called `whatever-min.js` which are used in production to reduce download times. If you want to play about with the javascript then I'd stick with the standard versions for the time being. I'm not sure how YUI is going to be plumbed into Moodle. Ideally you only want the parts that are used loaded, but you don't really want to go the route taken with CSS where different files are munged together as that would affect caching. Ideally you want a way to request that standard javascript library file x be linked from the header (but not add it twice if it is already requested) but also add random javascript, e.g. what is currently stashed in a script tag within the AJAX calendar block, too rather than have it inline. From what Jan says about `javascript.php` files within blocks the latter is possible but not the former. Within that framework it might be cool if turning on Moodle's debug mode swapped out the minimised javascript for the more verbose ones (I think some have actual 'debug' versions too)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Front page block only viewable after login
ResponsesInList.Text: Create a new block on the front page (you probably want an HTML block). Click the roles icon in the block header (visible when editing is turned on), and override the Guest role, setting moodle/block:view ("View block") = Prevent. This block will only be visible to users once they log in.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: install Gong in Apache server
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Apache2 is meant for CGI /PHP scripts + talking to databases (usually mySQL , Access, SQL Server or anything you can get an ODBC data connection to). Apache Tomact is designed for running java servlets, so it's unlikely you can get away from it (unless this Gong thing has a PHP version?) - if you have root/admin access to the server, your best bet is to install Apache Tomcat, make sure you have the mod_proxy + mod_proxy_ajp options installed/enabled then setup a proxy instruction the apache config file once you've setup Gong - bear in mind tomcat will need a separate port, but this doesn't need to be opened up to the outside world - as long as your apache server can see this port (eg if it's within same server or LAN) it should be ok. Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Default blocks viewable for all courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually you can specify which blocks to include as defaults for new course creations. The setting is not supported in the GUI but can easily be managed through the config.php file. If you look at the config-dist.php file included with the source, you will find all kinds of extra options not supported by the GUI. Several of them control which blocks are included by default when a new course is created. The option that specifies this for ALL courses looks like: $CFG->defaultblocks_override = 'participants,activity_modules,search_forums,admin:news_items,calendar_upcoming,recent_activity'; The colon simply separates the blocks that show up on the left and rights sides respectively. There are several other options that allow for more specific options such as default blocks for weeks type courses, topics type courses, etc. I would recommend looking over all the options in the config-dist.php file to get an idea of what extra control you may have outside of the GUI, I certainly found it helpful. Hope this helps dk

ResponsesInList.Title: MySQL statements inside blocks..
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everybody.. I have been developing a new search block for my university. I have implemented some fuctions that contains SQL select statements. but it always shows the following message : Warning : mysql_query() [ function.mysql-query ]: Access denied for user 'ODBC'@'localhost' (using password: NO) in C:\wamp\www\moodle\blocks\myBlock\mySearch.php on line 69 what do you think is the prblem and how can i solve this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MySQL statements inside blocks..
ResponsesInList.Text: You should not try to use your own connection. relying on the standard Moodle API for accessing the database will setup for you all the needed context to connect properly : get_records_xxx() function for selecting, including a get_records_sql($sql) where you can get almost what you want. insert_record($table, $record) for inserting an object/record delete_records_xxx() for deleting cout_records_xxx() for counting When your block code is visible in a course page, the course page did that setup for you. When you are coding an autonomous page of your block, allways include the top site config.php that will do the setup of the database connection, and use require_login() to check access and print_header(...) for generating the top header. Most of these functions are documented in http://phpdocs.moodle.org Search also in http://docs.moodle.org in the Developper documentation. You'll have clear documents on all this process.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Sandor, First of all we are very happy this block is maintained again!!! I think it's a very good idea to sort the items and to be able to hide those one doesn't need! Some comments: 1) Could you document how to migrate from course_menu 1.6 (Humboldt University) to 1.7 and then to 1.8? My experience: backup mdl_block and mdl_block_instance table to mdl_block_bak and mdl_block_instance. Uninstall course_menu from the administration menu, delete old course_menu folder from moodle/blocks (and language files if any from moodle/lang/en_utf8/block_course_menu.php and moodledata/lang/<language>/block_course_menu.php for the other languages). Install new course_menu (copy folder to moodle/blocks and languages to language directories, then go into administration, notifications). Run query that inserts the block where it was before in the courses, maybe even with the displaying options of your choice (order and hide items). For example, if you want the course_menu at the top left position: INSERT INTO mdl_block_instance (blockid, pageid, pagetype, position, weight, visible, configdata) SELECT b.id, bi.pageid, bi.pagetype, bi.position, bi.weight, bi.visible, '<configurationstring>' AS configdata FROM mdl_block_instance_bak bi, mdl_block_bak bb, mdl_block b WHERE bi.blockid = bb.id AND bb.name = 'course_menu' In our case (sections, then Control Panel, GradeBook, Calendar, Show all Sections) <configurationstring> = '' 2) I'm not quite sure what the "blog menu" is for, could you tell us? 3) I installed the course menu + on our test server and everything works fine. I don't understand why you can't have a Main Menu on course pages. There is certainly some obscure technical reason. You're not the first person to ask for this -- see MDL-4138 . Home > Resources > Our Story > Editing Resource > Window > check "Show the course blocks" checkbox ... The checkbox causes your resource page to have the same blocks as the main course page. You can't configure them independently of the main course page. That explains why you are also getting the Description block. This is not a solution. Maybe you should explain how you're using the Main Menu block, and maybe we can suggest an alternative. I'm happy to help if I can, but I think you're up against a fundamental limitation of Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle video tutorial: hiding a block from guests
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aaron, First of all, your video stands out amongst the others by its clarity. Your speech is deliberately slow and well pronounced, which makes your video very accessible. Another good point is that you go through each point without skipping over key elements. We can see where you're clicking, and what you're doing at all times. This makes it easy to reproduce your actions. Your video would have benefited from a small level of zoom, to make the text a little easier to read. Also, I'm not sure which method you chose for sound compression, but it cracks quite a bit. This doesn't distract too much though, I wouldn't worry much about it. The main point that needs work is your time management. Two segments in particular are needlessly long, with no commentaries, and basically add nothing to the learning experience of the viewer. The first one is the logging in as administrator, which takes 15 seconds. You could easily do this in a couple of seconds, even if this means having a browser tab ready in advance with the admin already logged in. The second segment is when you scroll down the permissions table. This takes a painful 14 seconds, at the end of which we could forgive the viewer for forgetting what you're scrolling down for You could just ctrl-pagedown to the bottom after explaining that this is what you're doing. Then don't forget to mention that you are clicking on the save button. It's not that obvious at this resolution. If you reduce these two segments you will bring your total video time to around 3 minutes, which is perfect, and you will teach the same amount of material with added effectiveness. Nevertheless, pending a little more feedback here I'm quite happy to tag this task as complete for you. Well done!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle video tutorial: hiding a block from guests
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aaron, Thanks for your video tutorial on hiding blocks from guests. I agree with Nicolas that it's very clear and easy to follow. However, the title of GHOP task 85 is "Record a video demonstrating how to hide a block from guests" rather than "....how to hide blocks from guests". I think your video would be more useful for Moodle admins if you demonstrated how to hide only one block (perhaps on the site front page ) by overriding permissions in the block, rather than how to hide all the blocks in a course. Doing so would also avoid the long course permissions table. How to hide a single block is a question which is occasionally asked here on moodle.org, but I've never come across anyone wanting to hide all the blocks in a course. Another small suggestion: I noticed at the end of the video you said "If you have any further questions, please be sure to post them in the comments section below." Rather than suggesting that comments should be added to the YouTube page, which nobody is going to check regularly , how about suggesting that people visit moodle.org for help and support. If you can implement my suggestions, as well as following Nicolas' time management advice, then I'm sure the resulting video will be a great help to Moodle admins. Best wishes and thanks for participating in GHOP.

Today I tried adding an RSS feed to the block, and the problem has come back.  Very slow page loads, and the HTML gets truncated at the point where the RSS block should appear.  The feed validates correctly when I test it, but it doesn't display, the block (and all the code after it) just dies.  I've tried searching the forums to see if there's a fix for this, but none of the things mentioned in the threads I've looked at have got it working.  I've got Error Reporting set to E_ALL in php.ini , but I'm getting no errors reported.  It doesn't seem to be theme-related, as I've got my theme set to Standard, and it's still not working. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Birthday block: I haven't got the block to show up any birthdays yet
ResponsesInList.Text: Monico - You have to use one of the formating options available: ISO Date format: %Y-%m-%d (default) USA Date format: %m.%d.%Y EUR Date format: %d.%m.%Y It will only work if you use the separators listed. Otherwise the date functions in SQL will not recognize that it is a date. 2007-10-16 (ISO format) is thus not the same as 2007/10/16. Similarly 10.16.2007 (USA format) is not the same as 10/16/2007. Let me know if you continue to have problems or questions about getting the birthday block working. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Birthday block: I haven't got the block to show up any birthdays yet
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes - Definitely get the import done and then we will get the birthdays working. Think about which way you want to go and let me know which way you decide. Also, make sure to do a dump of your database should you need to restore it before doing any direct manipulation of it. As I said, the easiest is to do the import and then create a custom user field called DOB (the default I believe) or Birthday or something along those lines. Then I would manually go in and look up the id of that newly created field in the mdl_user_info_field (presumably 1 - which is what I'll use in the query below) but it is worth making sure. Then assuming the data is in the skype field mdl_user table you will execute something along the lines of (which means I have not actually tested or tried it) INSERT INTO mdl_user_info_data (userid, fieldid, data) SELECT id, 1, skype FROM mdl_user WHERE skype IS NOT NULL; Sometimes before doing the actual insert - especially if I already have valid data in the table - I will just run the SELECT part and see if the number of records and the data looks like what I intended. In any case, that will take all of the data from mdl_user and copy it to the mdl_user_info_data table where the birthday block will be able to see it. Then, after you have verified everything is working the way you want, you can clear the skype field in the mdl_user table with something like: UPDATE mdl_user SET skype = '' WHERE skype IS NOT NULL; Let me know how it goes. If you run into trouble just let me know. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: New Oliver Library Search Block
ResponsesInList.Text: We use the Oliver software package for our library here at Monte. Our Librarian wished to add the Library search functionality into Moodle. So I made this simple block. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Oliver Library Search Block
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, As you can see from the post date of the previous article, this block is by no means "new" any more. I've had a look at the code (as it's something I'd quite like to incorporate too) and I've hacked it about a little to get it working properly here. I've attached my hacked version. You should only need to replace the file "block_oliver.php". When you've copied it over open it with a text editor. You'll see that I've replaced any obvious calls to database tables or variables that no longer exist, with fixed values. To customise it to your requirements just edit the following lines at the top of the file: $this->title = ' Oliver Search '; (whatever you want to name the block) $serverpath = ' http://caracal/oliver/gateway/gateway.exe '; (the location of your Oliver gateway.exe file.) You can also edit any of the other variables to customise it further. Hope this helps! Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blocks won't display after routine 1.8.2 cvs update
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, I just upgraded too and have the same problem. Traced the problem to some third party modules we're using: Turned on debugging: Site admin block > Server > Debugging > switched Debug messages to all and ticked Display debug messages. Switched on editing in a course and checked the debug messages which appeared on screen. Noticed that the Book and Questionnaire modules were mentioned in the error messages. Switched off the Book and Questionnaire: Site admin block > Modules > Activities and closed the "eye" next to the offending modules. Switched off debugging Not a great fix as we use the questionnaire a bit. But all I can do for now (doing upgrades late at night to avoid disrupting service). I think it may be a case of waiting for third party modules to be upgraded to work with 1.8. Maybe there's an easier fix, but reading a couple of other posts, it appears the problem affects several non-core modules.

ResponsesInList.Title: New SquirrelMail Block
ResponsesInList.Text: Here at my college our students access their webmail using an app called squirrelmail. Because we use LDAP , their logon details for moodle and SQM are exactly the same and allowed for me to create this block to allow for easy access. For security freasons we ask students to type in in their passowrd again rather than passing this info automatically. This decision was made as many students often forget to log out. And the last thing we wanted was for access to other students mailboxes due to this. Setup is easy. Just extract the zip to your moodle root and then go to admin to install the block. Once installed, go to Admin->Blocks-> SquirrelMail Block settings and enter the URL to your SQM installation. Then your done. I have set this up to use lang packs, but only speaking english have attatched only the en lang data. Hope some of you find this useful.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't get reset blocks
ResponsesInList.Text: The table mdl_block_instance holds information for the blocks displayed for a course where pageid=courseid. If you look at the table you'll probably get a better understanding of how it works than if I explain it but to reset blocks for a course just remove the entries for that course from the ml_block_instance table. Using DELETE FROM `mdl_block_instance` WHERE `pageid` = n; worked fine for both a single courseid or a range of courseids. I've got the default blocks set using site wide sticky blocks (using moodle 1.82+) so once i removed the entried in mdl_blocks_instance my preferred blocks were present (without any duplicates etc).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quickmail 1.8 problem -- Need help ASAP
ResponsesInList.Text: Albert, You are correct in that you must set the role capability for the quickmail block to show up for students. And I can explain exactly how to do this If you want to enable all students in all courses to be able to see/use the quickmail block, you must edit the global role capabilities. I believe A.T. covered this process above but I will go over it quickly: - navigate to Admin -> Users -> Permissions -> Define Roles - click the edit icon for the Student role - find the block/quickmail:cansend capability in the list (should be near the very bottom) - set this capability to allow instead of inherit This will enable all student in all courses to use/see the quickmail block To override the capability for specific course only: - Navigate to the course you wish to enable this block for - Click the 'Assign roles' link from the Admin block - from the tabbed links along the top of the roles screen, click the 'override roles' link - Click the Student role link - find the block/quickmail:cansend capability in the list (should be near the very bottom) - set this capability to allow instead of inherit Setting this capability allows students to see/use the quickmail block hope this helps, DK

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Birthday Block ?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Just a small issue. Using ... 
```text
$this->title = get_string('blockname','block_birthday');
```
 ... can confuse people who, for some reason, don't have all language packs installed. Instead of just `untranslated texts` , they will get real error messages about a naming conflict. People starting a new block are better of using a specific name, instead of the generic 'blockname': 
```text
$this->title = get_string('birthdays','block_birthday');
```
 A very minor issues, but I thought I should mention it before all of the different translations are already made and it would be difficult to undo them. Besides: most of the Naming conflict errors are about a block I started writing in which I also used the generic 'blockname' instead of a more proper name.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to delete a block?
ResponsesInList.Text: Halyna, It is unclear as to exactly what you would like to delete? Clarity is key in receiving accurate and helpful advice in forums such as this where the range of problems is never ending. It is possible to delete everything you mentioned in your post including: specific instances of blocks, entire block module from the Moodle system, and entire courses. to delete a block instance: Find the instance of the block you wish to delete (on a course page, front page , etc). Ensure that editing is on (you must have teacher/course creator/admin privileges). Then simply click the small X icon that appears in the title/header portion of the block. to remove the entire block module from Moodle system: navigate to Admin -> Configuration -> Blocks from the Admin block. A list of the installed blocks is displayed. To remove a type of block, simply click the 'delete' link for that block. This will effectively remove all instances of the block and as well as the possibility of adding new ones. Only use this option if you never intend to use that type of block ever again. to delete an entire course:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Any help v gratefully receiving on this: People block not appearing on Front page for students
ResponsesInList.Text: I did some research. In 1.6 there was a Site administration option "allusersaresitestudents" that had the default value "yes." That meant everyone was listed as a Participant on your front page. The option no longer exists in 1.8 (at least I cannot find it). Furthermore, the default behavior seems to have changed: Only users who have explicitly been assigned a role in the front page course now appear in the list. The only way I know to do this is as follows (caution: do this in 1.8, not in 1.7). Manually assign every user on your site the role of Student in course 1 (Site administration -> Front page -> Front page roles). Of course this is not a viable solution because it requires the admin to do a role assignment for every new user. Maybe someone else can suggest a better way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trouble with 'Trouble Ticket' Block
ResponsesInList.Text: I know it's almost a year later, but I've found a solution. In addtion to the fix in this post, which deals with closing a parenthesis set, you should also change the following lines (starting from line 13) in form.php: 13 optional_variable($name, ''); optional_variable($email, ''); optional_variable($subject, ''); optional_variable($comments, ''); 17 optional_variable($fromcourse); to read: $name = ''; $email = ''; $subject = ''; $comments = ''; $fromcourse = 0; $name = $_POST['name']; $email = $_POST['email']; $subject = $_POST['subject']; $comments = $_POST['comments']; $fromcourse = $_POST['fromcourse']; This has to do with the deprecated function optional_variable. The block assumed that the variables posted from the form were in the variables $name, $email, etc... so here were explicitly put them in there. Before assigning the values we assign defaults. I hope that helps people like me who couldn't find solutions elsewhere.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MyCourses Block: How do you remove 'enrol in another course'
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Ruth, I actually just finished resolving this issue for myself. I assume you are referring to the third-party MyCourses block and not the standard Course block. Removing the 'Enrol in another course' link is possible but only through editing the code manually, not through any setting/option available through the interface. Luckily, in case your not a coding whiz, the modification is a very simple one. If you navigate to the directory containing the files that determine how the block is generated (should be /moodlehome/blocks/myCourse/HTML_TreeMenu-1.2.0) there will be a file there called TreeMenu.php. Open this file and make the following changes: on line 659, you can either comment out or delete this line all together, it is simply retrieving the string to display as the link. on line 660, the link code is appended to the $html var which gets printed as content. You can remove the link by deleting the link and center tags which look like this:
wwwroot course \">$enrol
be sure not to delete the quote and semicolon at the end of the line which closes the string to be appended to $html

ResponsesInList.Text: Add the following line to config.php - $CFG->allowvisiblecoursesinhiddencategories = true; Create categories to place your courses into and hide the categories. Move your courses into the hidden categories. (You may want to check to make sure courses are still visible - click on the hidden category and see.) Courses should now be hidden from the front page , but available and visible to the enrolled users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can HIDE Available Courses from home page??
ResponsesInList.Text: It may even be more simple than that. If you want to remove the entire list of courses, you can do so here: Administration block -> Front Page -> Front Page Settings -> frontpage setting (list of 4 combo boxes) and frontpageloggedin . Set all these combo boxes to none . In Moodle 1.7, I believe that it goes like this: Administration block -> Appearance -> Front Page (and maybe) -> Front Page Settings Hope this is the issue at hand. Zachary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blocks won't delete (1.8 upgrade from 1.6.3+)
ResponsesInList.Text: ATW, I hope this helps you... It looks to me like you are being confused by Sticky Blocks. When you add a sticky block to your courses, you can't move them around or delete them from within the course. If you could follow these instructions, let me know if it works: Go to a course and determine which blocks you want removed. The ones that have no delete button when editing is on are Sticky Blocks. Now go to Appearance --> Sticky Blocks --> Course Page (dropdown) Or, just go to http://www.yourdomain.com /admin/stickyblocks.php?pt=course-view Delete all the blocks in there. When I first installed Moodle, I was like "Oooh, sticky blocks! I can use that to automatically add the basic blocks (administration, participants, course summary, etc.)! I promptly did so, and what do you know, but Moodle is smart enough to add all those blocks when you initially create a course (or, in your case, restore [or whatever you chose to do]). I ended up with duplicate blocks, same as you seem to have.

ResponsesInList.Text: БЛОК ОЦЕНЯВАНЕ / MARKING BLOCK Learning activitie sensor, tracker and reminder Hello M-r Darren Smith, We've installed Marking_block and optimmized the source code for version 1.5.4 stab . Also here is bg and en translation for this contribution of this marcking_block version we using in Bul gar ia DANIEL DENEV daniel_i_denev@abv.bg ИНСТАЛИРАНЕ: 1.разархивирате. Откривате съдържанието на папката blocks от архива. 2.След тованаправете резервно копие на папката blocks която се намира във вашата текуща инсталация. ОСНОВНО ПРЕДНАЗНАЧЕНИЕ Модулът предоставя информация на преподавателя за дейностите изискващи неговата намеса и оценяване. Включена е отделна страница за алтернативен електронен дневник с оценки. Блокът е наличан само за администратори и преподаватели. Блокът осигурява информация за последно изпратените работи, повторно изпратените, и закъснелите (дейности закъснели от зададената дата за завършване. Много полезен при оценка на тестове от тип есе например. Блокът показва списък с оценки и студенти. Блокът може да се конфигурира да показва определен брой студенти в списъка, както и успеха и развитието на всеки студент. Съществуват няколко общи функции в библиотеката които правят същото и следователно могат да се добавят нови дейности но ще се изисква писането на допълнителен код. MARKING BLOCK INSTALLATION: To install and use, unzip this file into your web root directory making sure that you 'use folder names'. This will add a new block directory (marking) to your '/blocks' directory and some language files to your langage directory. Once unzipped, visit your admin screen and configure the new block the way you want. MAIN PURPOSE The Marking block is a kind of block that provides a summary of activities awaiting grading. It includes a separate page that provides an alternate gradebook functionality ties to the marking block. This block is restricted to teachers and administrators. This block displays marking information for newly submitted, resubmitted, and overdue (activities past their defined close dates) activities. The marking page provides the same information and easy access to the grading functions for these activities. This block cam also display a list of students below a certain grade level. The block can be configured to display a maximum number of students in each list and to set the grade level to display below. This directory uses custom code for all activities it summarizes. There are few common activity library functions that can perform the same operations, and thus any new activities to be added will need new code. ХАРАКТЕРИСТИКИ И ФУНКЦИОНАЛНОСТ Блок за оценяване Преподавателят добавя курсове които иска да вожда и следи активността на обучаемите в тях. Той може да избере коя група в рамките на курса да се показва. Блокът е олекотен като е премахната излишната информация и размерите му са приемливи за първа страница. Страница за оценяване Допълнителен бутон съхранява всички рецензии на едно място Достъпни са линкове за обновяване на задачата в заданието или теста. Тези линкове са съхранени по първи изпратил зада чата си студент, а не по последен. Сензор за закъснение на дейност от преподавател или студент Маркиране за въпроси от тип кратък отговор в рамките на модула урок Маркиране в регион Всяко маркирано задание показва колко време е отнело на преподавателя (КОНТРОЛ НАД КАЧЕСТВОТО НА ОБУЧЕНИЕТО). Всяка с траница за оценяване на задание или тест показва средното общо време на групите студенти. Съществува бутон за автоматично следене и напомняне при закъсняване на студенти да си изпратят работите и преподавате ли закъсняващи с оценяването или някаква друга контролна дейност. Налично е поле за написване на стандартно съобщение за напомняне. Неизпратените задачи или непроведените други дейности са първи и маркирани по подразбиране. Часът и времето на известяването се съхраняват и активизират с настъпването на събитие в рамките на процеса. В блока се отчита броя на непроведените мероприятия, закъсненията и процентно съхранените FEATURES AND FUNCTIONALITY Front page marking block Teacher adds courses to display on front page marking block Teacher can select which group within courses to display Some information removed on front page to make the block a sensible size Marking Page An additional master button to save all feedback in one go Update assignment links Sorted by first student submission rather than most recent Indication of how late a submission is Marking for short answers in lessons Marking turnaround Each marked assignment shows how long it took the teacher to mark = TEACHING QUALITY MEASUR EMENT (marking date/time - student submission date/time) Every assignment marking page shows average turnaround time for groups Button to auto remind unsubmitted students Default message from teacher Unsubmitted checked as default Time and date of notification stored (so can also check how many notifications have been sent) Block Unsubmitted sorted by amount of unsubmitted Percentage sorted with highest first

ResponsesInList.Title: "Show Current Section" block
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all I've created a block that allows the user to toggle between showing the "current section" in a course, and the whole course. It mimics the behaviour of the "show all weeks/topics" and "show only week x/topic x" link in the top-right corner of each section. Just like these links, the last setting a user had in the course is preserved in the database , although the block itself does not create any new database tables. It is based substantially on the "Section Links" block that already exists in Moodle, so I'm not claiming a huge degree of original thought. It may prove useful to people with long course homepages, e.g. a course that spans multiple terms or semesters. Some notes: In a "weeks" format course, this block links to the current week. If the current week is hidden from the students, or if today's date does not fall within the range of the course, the block is not displayed. In a "topics" format course, the block links to the highlighted topic. If there is no highlighted topic, the block is not displayed. It uses has_capability(), so is only compatible with Moodle 1.7 or later. We've found that, position-wise, top-left or top-right makes the most sense to the user. Since I did it on school time, it is by definition copyright my Lords and Masters, but it is released under the GPL. Hope it proves useful. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding RSS Blocks in Moodle Build 1.7.1
ResponsesInList.Text: I have found a work around for this problem though I can't guaranteee it will work for everyone. Also, I can't tell you EXACTLY which extension is fixing the problem but it seems to be an extension problem. 1) download a copy of the XAMPP installation for your version of moodle, or the closest you can find. 2) Unpack the .zip folder and open the ‘php’ folder which can be found in there. 3) In there is a folder called ‘ext’ which holds the PHP extensions. 4) Copy the contents of this folder and paste them into the corresponding folder on the installation you want the RSS feeds on. I click ‘do not overwrite’ on all the duplicate files it found. There will be a few. 5) Next, go back into the XAMPP installation and open up the ‘php.ini’ file and so a search for the string ‘Windows Extensions’. Normally around line 563. A few lines under this there will be a number of lines which look a bit like this: ;extension=php_apd.dll ;extension=php_bcompiler.dll ;extension=php_bitset.dll ;extension=php_blenc.dll 6) Copy all the lines that look like this and paste them into the php.ini file in your big moodle install. Note: if you are using LDAP for your authentication, you’ll need to take the ‘;’ from the beginning of the line to uncomment it. 7) Restart your server or reset the moodle install and hey presto, it should be working. This worked for me not 20 minutes ago so I’m pretty confident it works. I’m not sure exactly which extension it is which is needed for the RSS feeds but by installing the full lot and defining it in the extensions area of PHP.ini, it fixed that problem for me. Do you think I should put this up on the Moodle forums? I’m sure people must have tried this before… Oh, as a side note, this seems to have sorted the RSS Problem in my Moodle 1.8 install too… Regards, Al

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: xml parsing error
ResponsesInList.Text:
I solved the problem. There is an unspoken rule in building blocks, there can be NO whitespace outside of the PHP tags!! so if this is your file: --------------------- |<? | | ... | |?> | --------------------- You cannot do this: --------------------- |<? | | ... | |?> | | | --------------------- That extra line prints out at the top of the page dropping the 
```text
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
```
 down a line and causing a problem on the browser's side. Only some browsers report this error. It really depends on the server and the browser whether this error is thrown. Peter

ResponsesInList.Text: Clark - Not to rain on the parade but while I like the idea of an amped version of Moodle some of the modules and blocks may be mutually exclusive or not necessarily compatible with one another. Also, many of them may require that other software be installed. I'm thinking in particular of integrations. In addition, such a version may have more security holes in it and putting it together seems to maximize the likelihood of some type of vulnerability. For security, I think the idea of searching for what you want and adding it piecemeal has some advantages. In other words, start with what we know works pretty well (ie, Moodle core) and then hack away and add bits and pieces at will. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Pimp my Moodle: All blocks and modules?
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think it's a good idea to encourage people to go overboard with non-standard blocks and modules. Just because a block or module works with your current version of Moodle, there's no guarantee it will work when you upgrade to a newer version of Moodle. The block or module author has typically moved on on to a new project and has no time for "maintenance." Someone else has to do it. So having too many non-standard blocks and modules almost guarantees a painful upgrade. In the worst case, you won't be able to upgrade. A good example is the MyFiles block, one of the most popular 3rd-party blocks. It stopped working in Moodle 1.7. Those of us who use it can't upgrade to Moodle 1.7 without breaking a lot of activities that depend on MyFiles.

ResponsesInList.Text: Valid, John, but maybe a group of Moodlers will work on that. And where there is a will, there is a way! Depends who jumps on the bandwagon, no? Have to wait and see if anyone wants to take it on. As a matter of fact, we still use 1.6.x at Aiken High School because of this issue. And, of course, some third party mods seem to break backups. That is frightening. In the end, some non-standard mods are worth it to us. We are heavy users, for example, of the book and feedback mods. Wonder if anyone else has any ideas about this. -- Art

ResponsesInList.Text: Third party blocks and modules (even some many of us assumed were "standard") are falling by the wayside because there are not enough developers to maintain them. Remember Journal? Exercise is the latest casualty . Its functionality was supposed to be subsumed by Workshop, but that project is also in Limbo, again because of human resources (see MDLSITE-116 ). I wouldn't be surprised to see Workshop fall by the wayside. IMO there are no equivalents of Journal (please don't say "online assignment") and Exercise. So if you are dependent on these, you have no alternative but to stay with Moodle 1.6. We need an apprentice program for Moodle developers!

ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, Baruch! I hope I am understanding what you are saying in your post above! Have you been using learning management systems (LMS) for a long time, or is Moodle the first LMS you have used? I have used a proprietary system and Moodle, and it seems to me that we have a lot more options with Moodle. Of course to take advantage of those, you have to have certain skills. Not so much programming (I don't generate any new code!) but the ability to work with files on a remote server and to read and follow technical instructions. (This is not meant as a criticism of yourself, please understand, but the recognition that there is a certain level of comfort you need to manage a moodle instance as an admin). With a proprietary system, you only have options that you purchase and the installation might be handled by your vendor. But you also might have to do your own installation of patches and updates. I would think that is quite a common scenario. Getting to your questions/points: I don't understand the default architecture of my newly created site. The front page has a 'Main Menu' with links to glossaries I've created. These are site-wide glossaries, yet, when I click on a course, I can't find a link to them. Under the activity pull-down, I can 'add a glossary ' but I don't want to create a new one, thank you very much. I just want a link to the existing ones. I think, in general, that you should see the main page and the courses you have created as separate units. They do not pass content to each other. The main page is really just course #1 with a few special formatting options. I can't think of an easy way to create an HTML block with all the links in it and copy that to each course unless you set up a complete course template and restore that to create all your new courses. I think there is often discussion of sharing content across courses, so you might want to make an account in the issue tracker and vote for some feature requests that you would like to see in future versions of Moodle! I also want a sidebar with a list of courses, so users don't have to navigate to the front page The "courses" block will give you the list of courses on the side. You can make that show up in every course if you use the "sticky blocks" options as admin. I couldn't tell if you had already tried that or not! The courses block is part of the standard moodle code. and a sidebar of the current course with all the topic sections (names, not numbers) very easy navigation I have used the course menu block for quite a while and did not have any problems installing it. Maybe you could be more specific about which part of the process you find most difficult? Then, maybe one of us could make a little video or something to explain it. Is your problem that you are installing the wrong version, or that it doesn't work? Or that you did not know where to put the files? Or that you did not know how to trigger the installation? It would help if you recounted the steps you DID take and where the process seemed to break down. Anyway, don't give up! atw

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How align the block title
ResponsesInList.Text:
Step 1 is not needed if you want to change the word 'Courses' to 'Profiles' everywhere it is used in Moodle. You can change the function back to... 
```text
class block_course_list extends block_list {


 function init() {


 $this->title = get_string('courses');


 $this->version = 2004111600;


 }
```
 Notice that it says get_string('course s ') not get_string('course'). That means in Step 2 you need to change string['course s '] not string['course']. In lang/en_utf8/moodle.php set 
```text
string['courses'] = 'Profiles'
```
 and it should work. If you want to only change the block, not other instances where the word 'Courses' might be used, then keep your changes in Step 1 and add the line 
```text
string['Profiles'] = 'Profiles'
```
 to lang/en_utf8/moodle.php. Also there is a language file for the Course List block in /lang/en_utf8/block_course_list.php. This file has a $string['blockname'] that is equal to 'Course List'. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Javascript problem in block & forums
ResponsesInList.Text: I've found that the forums will just strip out an javascript code in forum posts before they are displayed. The javascript can be in the database fine, but the php will strip it out. The same with stuff like iframes. In the Admin->Security->Site Policy there is the "Enable Trusted Content" setting: By default Moodle will always thoroughly clean text that comes from users to remove any possible bad scripts, media etc that could be a security risk. The Trusted Content system is a way of giving partcular users that you trust the ability to include these advanced features in their content without interference. To enable this system, you need to first enable this setting, and then grant the Trusted Content permission to a specific Moodle role. Texts created or uploaded by such users will be marked as trusted and will not be cleaned before display. I haven't fully tried it yet, but that is probably a place to start.

ResponsesInList.Text: I have completely removed the marking block from Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Marking Block and lost Grades
ResponsesInList.Text: I've seen this behavior before, and have stopped using the Marking Block in my Moodle site for this very reason. However, all is not lost. Either install the MySQL Admin plugin ( http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=13&rid=448 ) or use PHPMyAdmin to look through your database to find all entries without any date/time stamp or a date/time stamp in the timemarked field of the mdl_assignment_submissions table. Delete any assignments which have been given a grade of zero but have a blank timemarked (or 0, it's been a while, I don't remember). Once you delete those values you should have back all of your submissions. Then delete and remove the marking block and it will never happen again. This only happens when you actually click the link on the marking page and it duplicates the entries. Each time you click the link it duplicates the zeros. So, if you click on the link twice you'll get duplicate zeros each time. Really, really aggravating... Good luck, -Geof
